final_command: WMS_WORKLOAD_PRODUCTS=500 WMS_WORKLOAD_BINS=100 WMS_WORKLOAD_LOTS=2 WMS_WORKLOAD_OPEN_ORDERS=500 WMS_WORKLOAD_ACTIONS=25 WMS_WORKLOAD_REPORT=/tmp/stateset-wms-workload-large-final.json bash scripts/local-postgres.sh target/release/examples/workload
notes: Every executable was built with cargo build/run --locked --offline --release --example workload; one unchanged workload source was used for all runs.
Binary hashes were captured before the next executable replaced them. Complete baseline source was not captured with its executable; no baseline source digest is asserted.
The intermediate and final persistence digests identify the exact source measured before the next edit; final source matches the final qualification image inputs.
Earlier runs shared an isolated qualification PostgreSQL cluster with retained synthetic test data. The final run deliberately used a fresh disposable cluster with the final migrations.

Same larger workload configuration and independent correctness totals match across all three larger runs. Cluster cache/table population and shared-host scheduling differ, so the values are observations rather than controlled causal estimates.
Only one short measurement window per profile is retained; facility qualification should repeat expected peak workloads and enforce reviewed thresholds.
Reported process high-water memory includes setup and post-run verification, excludes PostgreSQL, and does not establish constant-memory behavior.
